s1.syndrome_frame: Intermittent palpitations with wide complex tachycardia and abnormal cardiac structure
salient_findings: Wide complex tachycardia at rate of 190 bpm
Grossly dilated RV with high RV end diastolic volume
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 20s
Complaints of intermittent palpitations for 2 days
Worsening of palpitations in the previous hour
No history of chest pain, dyspnea, congestion, or fever
No past cardiac history or family history of similar complaints
Blood pressure was 110/72 mm Hg
Respiratory rate was 14 bpm
ECG showed wide complex tachycardia with atypical left bundle branch morphology
QRS duration of 146 ms with no evidence of AV dissociation
Echocardiography showed global hypokinesia of right ventricle and dilated RV
Cardiac MRI showed grossly dilated RV and high RV end diastolic volume
Postcontrast hyperenhancement along RV free wall and other areas

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: ECG and imaging findings consistent with ARVC, including wide complex tachycardia, global hypokinesia of right ventricle, and dilated RV

shortlist.label: Ventricular Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Wide complex tachycardia on ECG, consistent with ventricular tachycardia

shortlist.label: Brugada Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: ECG findings of wide complex tachycardia with atypical left bundle branch morphology, and epsilon wave present in lead V4, suggestive of Brugada syndrome

shortlist.label: Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: ECG findings of wide complex tachycardia, and imaging findings of dilated RV and RVOT, consistent with RVOT tachycardia

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging findings of global hypokinesia of right ventricle, and postcontrast hyperenhancement along RV free wall, suggestive of myocardial inflammation

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG, echocardiography, and cardiac MRI results all point towards significant right ventricular dysfunction and structural abnormalities, which are characteristic of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC). The presence of a wide complex tachycardia, global hypokinesia of the right ventricle, dilated RV, and postcontrast hyperenhancement along the RV free wall and other areas are all consistent with ARVC.

rejected.label: Ventricular Tachycardia
rejected.why: While the patient presented with ventricular tachycardia, this is a symptom rather than a diagnosis and can be a manifestation of underlying conditions such as ARVC.

rejected.label: Brugada Syndrome
rejected.why: Brugada Syndrome typically presents with a specific ECG pattern characterized by ST elevation in leads V1-V3, which is not mentioned in the case description.

rejected.label: Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Tachycardia
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a narrower QRS complex and is often associated with a more benign prognosis than what is suggested by the patient's imaging findings.

rejected.label: Myocarditis
rejected.why: Myocarditis would likely present with more systemic symptoms such as fever and chest pain, and the imaging findings would not be as specific to the right ventricle as seen in this case.
